summary: Highlands County tower on Wales Ridge beside Archbold Biological Station; a 100 ft Aermotor LS-40 registered in 2016, last regularly staffed in 1999. Build date not found.

access.note: Enclosed by a security fence; the register describes no public access or climbing rules.

facts.agency: Florida Department of Agriculture & Consumer Services

events.note: Last regularly staffed in 1999, according to the register entry
Registered July 24, 2016 as US 1081, FL 15; nominated by Robert Spear

evidence.supports: Tower on Wales Ridge close to Archbold Biological Station, overlooking the Everglades headwaters
evidence.quote: Located on Wales Ridge (the north-south backbone of Florida) close to Archbold Biological Station, the Archbold Fire Tower overlooks the headwaters of the Everglades.
It was last regularly staffed in 1999.

notes_for_editor: No build date, designer, cost or design history for the tower was found in two searches and about five page reads. The station history covers the Red Hill buildings (designed and built 1930-1935 by Alexander Blair) and does not mention a tower. The NRHP record for the station (NRIS 07000698) mentions no tower. The record's elevation_m 65.2 is the NHLR ground elevation (214 ft), not tower height; height_m 30.5 is the register's 100 ft converted, and the cab-floor height is not stated. Staffing as_of 2016 is the register date; 1999 is the last regular staffing. A towerdex entry for a Highlands County structure in Venus was seen in search results but is unverified and not cited. The travel-blog 'water tower' at the station is not a fire lookout. Visit: no climbability or trail info found.
